query: What visit-note signals suggest a longer visit?

per_column.name: note_length_chars
per_column.rationale: Character length of the note is a generic text feature, but it lies outside visit_duration and can plausibly correlate with visit complexity/length. Weak but legitimate predictor, not a restatement or leak.

per_column.name: sentence_count
per_column.rationale: Another generic verbosity feature; independent of duration and may weakly track visit complexity. Legitimate but low-signal predictor.

per_column.name: medical_term_count
per_column.rationale: Count of medical terminology reflects clinical complexity of the encounter, which plausibly drives longer visits. Outside the focus and carries genuine domain signal.

per_column.name: comorbidity_count
per_column.rationale: Number of comorbidities mentioned is a substantive clinical predictor of visit length; more comorbidities typically require longer visits. Not derivable from duration.

per_column.name: action_count
per_column.rationale: Count of clinical actions/procedures noted plausibly increases visit time. It is a driver of duration rather than a restatement of it, so a legitimate predictor. Borderline: actions are contemporaneous with the visit, but they are causes of time spent, not a deterministic function of the recorded duration.

per_column.name: multi_complaint_flag
per_column.rationale: Indicator of multiple presenting complaints is a clear complexity signal that plausibly predicts longer visits. Independent of the focus variable.

judge.rationale: All six columns lie outside visit_duration_min, none restate or leak it, and each plausibly carries some predictive signal. The strongest domain-grounded features are medical_term_count, comorbidity_count, action_count, and multi_complaint_flag, which capture clinical complexity that genuinely drives visit length. note_length_chars and sentence_count are generic verbosity features with weaker, partly redundant signal. As a set they provide meaningful but moderate predictive leverage beyond the original columns, hence a mid-range utility rather than high.
